item.title: Fixtures and standings as Nations Championship returns
item.description: The Nations Championship resumed on Friday with Ireland securing a 42-12 win over Argentina, as the battle for continental supremacy heats up. After three rounds of home games for southern hemisphere nations in July, the northern hemisphere teams are the hosts for the final three rounds. Ireland's win moved them top of the northern standings until France thrashed Fiji 54-17 on Saturday to regain their lead with 17 points from four matches. Scotland were outclassed by New Zealand in the second half and are in third place in the northern table following a 43-21 defeat at Murrayfield. Fourth-placed England have 10 points and play Australia - who are third in the southern standings - at Allianz Stadium on Sunday. Wales overcame Japan 28-21 to move level on points with England but have a vastly inferior points difference. Bottom-side Italy, who lost all three of their away games in the summer, were outgunned 66-7 by South Africa on Saturday. The Springboks continue to lead New Zealand on points difference, with both teams having won all four of their games with bonus points. The world champions face Six Nations champions France in a huge game in Paris on Friday. The Nations Championship pits the northern hemisphere teams who compete in the Six Nations - England, Ireland, Scotland, Wales, France and Italy - against southern hemisphere giants South Africa, New Zealand, Australia and Argentina, plus invited sides Fiji and Japan. All teams will play each of the six in the opposing hemisphere once, with three rounds of fixtures staged in July and another three in November. Their results will rank the teams within their own hemisphere, from one to six. On the final weekend in November, there is a three-day play-off event staged at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham. The sixth-placed team in the northern hemisphere plays off against the equivalent in the southern hemisphere standings and so on, culminating in the two top-ranked sides taking each other on. The winner of that final match is crowned the inaugural Nations Championship winner. There is also a parallel, Ryder-Cup style hemisphere title. item.title: Jordan Love, Drake Maye represent new era in Packers-Patriots matchup
item.description: The Green Bay Packers and New England Patriots don’t play each other that often. The most recent time was in 2022, an overtime game at Lambeau Field won by Green Bay with Aaron Rodgers under center during his final season in Green Bay. In the teams’ most recent matchup in New England in 2018, Tom Brady was on the field playing in his penultimate season with the team. Sunday’s game between the Packers (5-3) and Patriots (5-3) won’t feature either future Hall of Famer. Rodgers is playing what he’s said is his final NFL season in Pittsburgh, and Brady will be calling his first game in Gillette Stadium as an analyst for Fox Sports. “I think I’m required contractually to catch up with him at some point,” Patriots coach Mike Vrabel joked this week about Brady’s latest return to New England. But there will be plenty of focus on the quarterbacks that have come behind Rodgers and Brady for their respective former franchises. Jordan Love appears to be finding his stride in his fourth season as the full-time starter, leading the league in passing yards for a team looking to make the playoffs for the fourth consecutive season. Meanwhile, Drake Maye has recovered from a rough start to account for at least three touchdowns in each of his past five games, leading the Patriots to victories in four of them. While the Packers enter the game last in the NFL in rushing, averaging only 60.6 yards per game, Love said he isn’t worried about generating offense. “The run game isn’t where it needs to be, but I think we’ve still been able to kind of adjust and still make plays,” he said. “There’s a lot more out there, but we’ve done a great job just being able to win these games by putting up some points, and that’s what it comes down to.” Maye said the matchup is certainly a measuring stick opposite a team that like them is trying to keep pace in their division. “They’re good, they’ve beaten good teams, and they continue to show up every year,” Maye said. “We’ve definitely got a challenge and a chance to see how we look.” Need to know Green Bay (5-3) at New England (5-3) When/where to watch: Sunday, 4:25 p.m. EST, FOX. Last meeting: Packers beat Patriots 27-24 on Oct. 2, 2022, in Green Bay. Series record: Packers lead 7-6. Matchup to watch Packers QB Jordan Love vs. Patriots secondary. The Packers quarterback is leading the NFL with 2,246 passing yards (280.8 per game) to go along with 16 touchdown passes (fourth in the NFL). item.title: What activating Mack Hollins means for the Patriots
item.description: The writing was on the wall, and on Saturday the New England Patriots made it official. Mack Hollins has returned to the team’s 53-man roster after spending the previous four weeks on its injured reserve list; the veteran wide receiver was sent there after sustaining a calf injury in Week 4 versus the Buffalo Bills. Let’s assess what Hollins’ activation means for the Patriots ahead of their Week 9 contest versus the Green Bay Packers. Better depth Despite returning to practice earlier this week to open his 21-day window to return from injured reserve, Hollins initially remained on the list. While this is standard procedure — teams want to take a look at players at practice first before making any decisions regarding activation — it did leave the Patriots potentially three top-level wide receivers short heading into the weekend. Romeo Doubs remains on IR with a shoulder injury, while A.J. Brown was ruled out for a second straight game due to a knee issue. Had Hollins missed Sunday’s game as well, Drake Maye’s supporting cast would again have looked suspect, particularly considering running back TreVeyon Henderson’s medical status and tight end Hunter Henry being questionable for the contest as well. Hollins cannot patch all of those holes by himself, but having him available does upgrade New England’s overall defensive depth. Roster shakeup With Hollins back on the 53-man team, the Patriots now have five wide receivers rostered . In addition, their practice squad features three wideouts — one of whom, Ryan Miller, was elevated to the game day roster against the Miami Dolphins last week. 53-man roster (5): A.J. Brown (1), Mack Hollins (13), DeMario Douglas (3), Kyle Williams (18 | KR), Efton Chism III (86) Practice squad: Kyle Dixon (83), Chandler Brayboy (81), Ryan Miller (11) Injured reserve: Romeo Doubs (87) On paper, the Patriots are nearing full strength at the position again. That is particularly true given that Doubs will be eligible to come off IR himself after New England’s trip to Germany next week. The expectation is that he too will rejoin the active roster sooner rather than later, giving the club a full complement of wideouts again. That said, A.J. Brown’s status remains a question mark. While the team is optimistic that he will return before the end of the month, his participation in the upcoming international game against the Detroit Lions is uncertain. Trickle-down effect After Hollins exited the game against the Bills, one player in particular took on a bigger role: second-year man Efton Chism. item.title: Nebraska HC Matt Rhule has suffered losing streak since appearing on HBO hit Lanterns
item.description: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images Nebraska head coach Matt Rhule made an appearance as himself on HBO and DC Studios’ show Lanterns last month, but his record since then hasn’t been great. Rhule played himself in the hit show, making an appearance in the final episode of the season while trying to recruit a character on the show. However, this one-time appearance in Hollywood may have jinxed his Cornhuskers, who haven’t been able to win a game since his cameo. Nebraska Cornhuskers go 0-4 after Matt Rhule’s appearance on HBO’s Lanterns After their latest loss to Illinois, one fan on social media pointed out that the Nebraska Cornhuskers have lost four games straight since Matt Rhule made an appearance on HBO and DC Studios’ hit show. In the show, Matt Rhule is there to help recruit Noah Macon to Nebraska as their next quarterback, not knowing that he was a half-alien being known as a manhunter. Macon, who was initially portrayed as a possible future villain, tells John Stewart that he wishes to lead a normal life and not fulfil his programming’s goal to take over humanity. In the canon of the DC Universe, Matt Rhule is pivotal to the future safety of the human race, as he will be one of the figures guiding and mentoring a manhunter with the power to take over the entire planet. However, that will come as little relief to Rhule and the rest of the Cornhuskers, given their woes this season. After their loss to Illinois, Rhule decided to fire OC Dana Holgerson, marking the first major personnel change he and the Cornhuskers have had to make. The Cornhuskers are currently 5-4 for the season, squandering what had been a solid 5-0 start to the season over the last month. Within the Big Ten, the Cornhuskers are 2-4, showing that they are far from being able to compete against the best of the best in their conference. item.title: Today in White Sox History: November 8
item.description: Joe Nossek, who did a little bit of everything during two coaching tenures with the White Sox, was born on this day, 86 years ago. | (Photo by Ron Vesely/Getty Images) 1920 For a few days, the White Sox were members of the National League. With many owners dissatisfied with the National Agreement (governing the game, the majors, the minors, and all baseball commerce), 11 clubs hatched a plan to form a new National League — a single league including every team. Included in this “Allied Eleven” were the White Sox. With all 16 MLB teams gathering at the Congress Hotel in Chicago, the “Allied Eleven” met in one room and “Loyal Five” (to the American League, consisting of Cleveland, Detroit, the Philadelphia A’s, St. Louis Browns and Washington) another, with Senators owner Clark Griffith shuttling between the two rooms as messenger. When agreement couldn’t be struck to keep the AL-NL MLB dynamic going, the White Sox, Yankees and Red Sox all resigned from the AL and joined the National League. Cooler heads prevailed four days later, with the leagues remaining intact and the approval of Kenesaw Landis as baseball’s first commissioner was a key part of a redrawn National Agreement. The decisions and changes made at these 1920 meetings largely define the structure of baseball today, more than 100 years later. 1940 Joe Nossek , longtime White Sox coach over two stints in Chicago, was born, in Cleveland. He first joined Tony La Russa’s staff from 1984 to 1986, and returned for a much longer stint that represented his last work in the majors, from 1991-2003. Nossek was a bench coach during some of his second tenure with the White Sox, but was known as an “eye in the sky” coach, specializing in stealing signs from opponents. Nossek honed his bird-dogging skills as a seven-year outfielder in the majors, suiting up for the Twins, A’s and Cardinals. 1977 The upstart South Side Hit Men, who led the AL West for about a third of the season and took baseball by storm in peaking at 25 games better than .500, were laid to rest with the loss of outfielder and folk hero Richie Zisk , who signed a 10-year, $2.3 million deal with the Texas Rangers . Zisk was the lone All-Star for the White Sox in 1977, finishing seventh on the club with 2.7 WAR, and fifth among hitters. His 30 home runs were second on the team; among them one ball on the Comiskey Park roof and another in its center field bleachers, rare feats both. Zisk duplicated his All-Star selection in Texas in 1978, but never again came close to the production he put up for the White Sox. He was out of baseball with four seasons still remaining on his contract. Losing Zisk spotlighted the down side of owner Bill Veeck ’s desperate Rent-a-Player concept, as star relievers Terry Forster and Goose Gossage had been shipped out to secure just one year of the slugger. 1999 South Carolina Rep. item.description: DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 3: Aaliyah Crump #7 of the Duke Blue Devils prepares to shoot a free throw during Countdown to Craziness at Cameron Indoor Stadium on October 3, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Lance King/Getty Images) | Getty Images T here’s a bit of a strange situation for Duke Women’s Basketball right now. Originally scheduled to play North Texas in San Antonio, hometown of Arianna Robertson and Bella Flemming, the game was canceled. According to Raleigh’s News & Observer, Duke put out this statement: “Due to circumstances beyond the control of the participating institutions, the women’s basketball game between Duke and North Texas scheduled for Nov. 8 in San Antonio will not be played.” Duke scrambled to fill the spot and will be playing FAU instead. The Owls will now play Saturday and Sunday, which is obviously tough, but given the situation, FAU may get a financial bonus. Duke tried to sell a home game but found no takers. It’s possible that Florida Atlantic may get a bonus out of it, but that hasn’t been announced if so. No one has said specifically what happened, but Duke and North Texas seem to be on the same side, with nearly identical statements, so you get the sense that the organizers of “The Foundry Classic” screwed up somehow. All’s well that ends well, more or less, but now the Blue Devils will pay an unfamiliar opponent on short notice and with little preparation. item.title: Rory McIlroy comments on Patrick Reed and Eugenio Chacarra when asked about Race to Dubai chances
item.description: Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images Rory McIlroy finished in third place this week at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, keeping his outside chances of winning the Race to Dubai for an eighth time alive. McIlroy played some exceptional golf this week at Yas Links, but he was far too inconsistent to challenge Jon Rahm in the end. The Northern Irishman made 29 birdies and one eagle in Abu Dhabi, but he also made a quadruple bogey, a double bogey and six bogeys. Rory McIlroy is still in with a shout of winning the Race to Dubai and he will be in the final group out alongside Eugenio Chacarra at The 2026 DP World Tour Championship on Thursday. He leap-frogged Patrick Reed into second place in the standings this week. And the six-time major champion has now opened up on how he feels about his chances of winning the season-long race next week in Dubai. Rory McIlroy comments on Patrick Reed and Eugenio Chacarra when asked about Race to Dubai McIlroy spoke to reporters after his final round in Abu Dhabi on Sunday. The Northern Irishman was asked whether he is content with his position in the Race to Dubai standings heading into the final event of the season next week in Dubai. “ Yeah, absolutely. That’s where I wanted to be, “ McIlroy replied. “ It’s a pretty familiar spot for me going into The DP World Tour Championship, and I’m excited for it. That was the goal coming into these two weeks to try to catch Eugenio and Patrick and try to win The Race to Dubai again. “ Yeah, it would have been great to win this week and give myself not as much of a deficit or even a lead, but I still feel like I’m right in there with a great chance. “ McIlroy then delivered his verdict on his performance this week at Yas Links. “ It was sort of a week where I felt like I had my chances, “ he admitted. “ You know, especially today, birdieing 10 and 11 on the back to get tied for the lead, and then I had two good chances, 12 and 13, and didn’t make those. Had to scramble for par on 14. And then, yeah, I just couldn’t keep my momentum going. “ But it was a good week. I saw some encouraging signs in the game. You know, I’m going to be in that final group going out on Thursday next week. So yeah, I obviously would have loved to have won the tournament, but enough positive signs to feel good about going into next week. “

item.title: NHL goalies from your nightmares: 5 all-time most frightening netminders in crease
item.description: Scoring a goal in the NHL is hard enough on any night. But going up against certain goalies was a total nightmare. These guys didn’t just stop pucks; they made the game feel like a street fight, messed with shooters’ heads and made players think twice before skating anywhere near the net. Some of them were straight-up bullies in the crease. If you got too close, you were getting slashed on the ankles, shoved or pulled into a brawl. Others relied on pure mind games, whether it was wearing creepy masks or using wild, unpredictable styles that made no sense but always worked. Just having them in net was enough to throw opposing players completely off their game. MORE: 3 NHL teams that should be worried after tough starts to 2026-27 season Best of all, they had the talent to back it up. They weren’t just goons in pads; they were champions. They lifted Stanley Cups, took home major awards, and came up with huge saves whenever their teams needed them. From bloody on-ice fights to mind-bending saves, these netminders left a serious mark on hockey history. Here are five goalies who truly terrified the players standing across from them. 5. Dominik Hasek: Unorthodox nightmare for shooters Buffalo Sabres goalie Dominik Hasek (39) on the ice against the New York Islanders at Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum. Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Dominik Hasek earned the nickname “The Dominator” by making saves that seemed impossible. His style looked chaotic compared with the techniques most NHL goalies use. He dropped his stick, rolled onto his back and threw his legs into the air to stop shots. For opposing forwards, predicting his next move was often a losing battle. Hašek’s numbers explain why his unusual approach worked so well. He recorded a career save percentage of .9223, the highest in NHL history among goaltenders who played more than 500 games. He also won the Vezina Trophy six times (1994, 1995, 1997, 1998, 1999 and 2001). The two-time Stanley Cup winner’s achievements went beyond goaltending awards. Hašek remains the only goalie in NHL history to win the Hart Memorial Trophy twice. His unpredictable saves and remarkable consistency made him a nightmare for even the league’s best scorers. 4. item.title: Red Sox Get Realistic Report on Chances of Landing Tarik Skubal
item.description: Red Sox Get Realistic Report on Chances of Landing Tarik Skubal originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Red Sox have needs on both sides of the baseball, but it's obvious that the front office is likely going to focus on the offensive side of things. If the Red Sox make the necessary moves during Major League Baseball's offseason, whether it be in free agency or the trade market, they should find themselves in a very good position to be one of the best teams not only in the American League but in all of baseball. Last season was somewhat difficult to evaluate for the Red Sox because at times they looked like one of the best teams in the game, but at other times they looked about average. There's obviously a lot of hope that the Red Sox will be that team day in and day out like they were for much of the big stretch a season ago, but that might be an unrealistic ask. Regardless, the easiest way to get there is to add players who can help them improve. At the top of that list would be Tarik Skubal, undoubtedly the best player on the free agent market. While Skubal would be a dream addition, the latest report suggests it's unlikely. “The Red Sox are likely to focus on improving their offense first and foremost, but there’s no such thing as too much pitching depth, so adding a middle-to-back-end starter is on the table. At the moment, the Red Sox possess a full rotation with Garrett Crochet, Ranger Suarez, Payton Tolle, Jake Bennett and Brayan Bello or Tanner Houck, but adding to that group will fortify against the inevitable injury. “While it’s not out of the question that the Red Sox try to reunite with Sonny Gray or target higher-end starters like Freddy Peralta or Trevor Rogers, it’s unlikely the Red Sox will be dropping $400 million to sign Tarik Skubal,” Jen McCaffrey wrote . A lot of this is going to come down to the type of money that Skubal will land on the free agency market. While the Red Sox could realistically give him that type of money, it doesn't make a whole lot of sense to pay one player $400 million when there are some needs on both sides of the baseball. I wouldn't hate the Red Sox landing Skubal because of how talented he is, but I also recognize it could create another hole that wouldn't be filled. item.description: Real Madrid youngster continues to impress Mourinho with outstanding all-round display against Valencia Real Madrid’s impressive resurgence under Jose Mourinho continued at Mestalla , with Los Blancos securing a 3-0 victory over Valencia. Mourinho’s men secured their eighth consecutive victory , with their performances improving with every passing game. Federico Valverde, Arda Guler and Kylian Mbappe scored the goals for Los Blancos , while Yan Diomande delivered another encouraging performance. According to MARCA (h/t RM4Arab ), the Ivorian’s growing defensive commitment has been particularly impressive as Mourinho continues to rely on him more and more. Diomande impresses with his defensive commitment One particular moment in the Valencia game underlined exactly how the 19-year-old can contribute to the team. Diomande sprinted nearly 30 metres to stop an opposition counter-attack. It was precisely the kind of effort Mourinho has been demanding from his attacking players. Yan Diomande has performed very well in Vinicius Jr.’s absence. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Diomande’s statistics were equally impressive. The youngster won 12 duels, completed six of his eight attempted dribbles, drew three fouls and succeeded in all three defensive tackles. He has now completed 37 dribbles in La Liga this season, placing him second behind Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal, who leads the standings with 43. His dribbling success rate of approximately 65% further demonstrates the consistency with which he has been troubling opposition defenders. Vinicius’ return presents Mourinho with a dilemma Diomande’s emergence has been particularly significant during Vinicius Junior’s four-match domestic suspension. The youngster has established himself as a serious option on the left wing at a time when the Brazilian is not in great form. How does Mourinho handle Vinicius’ minutes in the upcoming fixtures?. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Vinicius will be available for selection after the international break, having served his suspension. This leaves Jose Mourinho with an important decision over how to handle a superstar like Vinicius. The Portuguese manager could retain Diomande on the left or accommodate both players by moving the youngster to the opposite flank. What makes the situation especially interesting is that Diomande is increasingly offering more than attacking contributions. One of the biggest issues with Vinicius has been his reluctance to track back, and Mourinho’s team look more balanced with Diomande in it. It remains to be seen how Mourinho handles this situation and whether Diomande has done enough to displace Vinicius from the starting XI after the break.

item.title: Liverpool do not want to rush decision on Barcelona loanee despite talks over January move
item.description: Liverpool do not want to rush decision on Barcelona loanee despite talks over January move Ronald Araujo has been nothing short of a revelation in the Premier League, ever since his loan move to Liverpool in the summer. The Uruguayan international, often labelled as an error-prone defender, has fit in incredibly well at Anfield, notably becoming a regular starter in the right-back position. Araujo even won the Liverpool player of the month award in November , with many now believing that the Reds will trigger his €55 million buyout clause. Liverpool in no rush All eyes on Ronald Araujo’s progress at Liverpool. (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images) However, a recent report from Diario SPORT has offered some updates on the future of Araujo. The report suggests Liverpool are in no hurry to make a decision as far as Araujo’s future is concerned. They do not want to activate the buyout clause just yet. The season is long, and the club are looking to wait until the latter part of the season before making any decision. As things stand, given the defender’s current form, Liverpool would be more than happy to pay €55 million to acquire the services of the on-loan Barcelona defender. This comes on the back of recent reports that suggest Liverpool have held talks with Barça over a potential January transfer for Araujo. It was suggested that the Reds were willing to activate the clause in the winter transfer window, but that is not the case, for now. Araujo aware of Barcelona interest Araujo is thriving in the Premier League. (Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images) Araujo, for his part, is also not thinking too much about his future at Liverpool for now and is focusing solely on his development. He knows that Barcelona are closely monitoring his progress. Given his affection for the club, one can be forgiven for thinking he would want to prove doubters wrong by coming back to Catalonia. Barcelona, for their part, could have used the services of Araujo given the club’s ongoing injury crisis in the defensive unit. That being said, it does seem likely that Araujo will be headed to Liverpool permanently next season. What remains to be seen is whether he can remain fit and continue his solid performances at the back.

item.title: Ole Miss fans cause delay for throwing trash in loss to Georgia
item.description: The Georgia Bulldogs came ready to play on Saturday night against the Ole Miss Rebels. Georgia raced out to a 14-0 first quarter lead and a 28-0 lead in the contest. Georgia snapped a 16-game Ole Miss home winning streak and got some revenge for losing to the Rebels in the Sugar Bowl last season. Georgia appeared to get a few favorable calls in the contest including a roughing the passer penalty and a pass interference penalty. The pass interference call drew heavy boos from the Ole Miss crowd. Some Ole Miss fans threw objects on the field following the call in the first half. That was about the only thing slowing down the Georgia offense all night. The trash on the field caused a significant delay in the game. Georgia was up 21-0 at that point with a little over five minutes left in the second quarter. The delay did not stop Georgia's momentum. Players walked toward the middle of the field to be out of the range of fans throwing objects during the delay. This is the third Georgia road game where opposing fans have thrown trash on their own field following a perceived missed call. A fine and potential bans for the fans responsible could be what happens next for the Ole Miss fans that participated in the incident. Today, we look at one of the most improbable, incredible months in baseball history. On the final day of August, the hottest hitter in all of Major League Baseball, Mickey Gasper, returned to the Red Sox lineup after a brief, and unnecessary, detour. Upon his return, he did what he had been doing the entire month. He homered, immediately, in the bottom of the first inning to tie the game against the Mariners at 1-1. Was Barry Bonds also the first player in history to balloon to a Size 9 hat during April of 2004? Almost certainly. You can take everything on there with a grain of salt. item.title: Bayern offer mixed updates on Kompany, Neuer and Musiala
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany pictured ahead of the German Bundesliga soccer match between FC Augsburg and Bayern Munich at WWK-Arena. (is associated with: «Bayern offer mixed updates on Kompany, Neuer and Musiala») Tom Weller/dpa Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will be back in two or three weeks after illness, the club's honorary president Uli Hoeness said on Sunday, while also voicing concerns about Jamal Musiala's health problems and what it means for the German double winners. Kompany collapsed during training just over two weeks ago and was taken to hospital, where doctors diagnosed meningeal irritation. Assistant coach Aaron Danks has stood in for him for five games, winning four and drawing one. "After the international break, in two or three weeks, he will be back on the bench," Hoeness told broadcaster Bayerischer Rundfunk. Leaders Bayern won 2-1 at Mainz in the Bundesliga on Saturday and due to the international break do not play again until hosting Cologne on November 20. Kompany was widely expected to be back then, but Hoeness suggested that date might come a bit too soon. "I think that was a very bad, neglected flu," Hoeness added. "He is under total stress. He works 12 hours a day, six days a week. That was simply too much." Head of sport Max Eberl had sounded a different tone shortly after Kompany's diagnosis: "It is an illness. Any one of us can get it. It has nothing to do with the pressure we face in the Bundesliga." Neuer and Musiala worries Bayern have been beset by illness and injury this season, with goalkeeper Manuel Neuer being the latest to be hurt when he was substituted for Jonas Urbig in the first half at Mainz. He became Bayern's oldest ever Bundesliga player aged 40 years and 225 days old, but a recurring partial tendon tear in his foot now rules him out for the foreseeable future, the club said on Sunday. This is expected to be his last season and Urbig is already primed as his successor. Playmaker Jamal Musiala is making his way back from a hamstring problem having begun the season by suffering two collapses in friendlies due to absence seizures. Doctors have said the Germany international can continue his career with little impact from the neurological issue, but Hoeness acknowledged the club have a quandary. "We are of course in a dilemma there," he said. "He has an illness that is not easily curable, but can be controlled to some extent with medication. But whether he will ever again have the performance level he once had... "But now he is still getting paid. Just imagine if Bayern were now to question his contract and say: what he can now deliver is no longer what was in the contract." The 23-year-old's bumper deal runs until 2030.

item.title: Discussion: How different do you expect the Panthers defense to look today?
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 15: Carolina Panthers defensive line coach Todd Wash looks on during the first half of the game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium on October 15, 2023 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images The last discussion post I put up asked about the warmth of Ejiro Evero’s seat. He’s been fired in the meantime, so I’d say it was pretty hot. It comes after an okay performance against the Green Bay Packers, but that’s probably more a product of convenience than anything. The Panthers were on a short week, so if the decision was made after the Buccaneers game, it would make more sense to wait a few extra days and make the move after the Thursday night game. In Ejiro’s place is Todd Wash. Wash overlapped with Dave Canales in Seattle in 2011 and 2012. He spent time as defensive coordinator in Jacksonville and led three units that were top six in yards allowed per game before things unraveled under Doug Marrone. He’s been the defensive line coach in Carolina since 2023 and was retained when Canales was hired in 2024. Now he gets his shot at defensive coordinator. He’s talked about changing the approach a little bit, and today’s discussion questions centers around that idea. How different do you expect the defense to look in the first week under Todd Wash? MY TAKE: I think we’ll see a difference for a couple of different reasons. First, the approach is supposed to be different under Wash. Not in a 4-3 vs 3-4 way, which seems to be an obsession of reporters for some reason, but rather a proactive mentality rather than a reactive one. From everything I’ve gathered, Evero preferred his defensive line to try to read the play before making a move. This often requires the linemen to absorb blockers before attempting to make a play. Wash has said he wants the line to be more proactive, which would mean prioritizing breaking the line of scrimmage first and then making a play. In his first press conference, Wash said the latter is what a lot of the linemen here played before they got to Carolina. He avoided saying it outright, but the implication is that this more aggressive approach on the line is a better fit for the personnel. On top of that, there are few better ways to galvanize a group of players than to fire their leader. Whether they were fans of Evero or not, the boss getting fired puts everyone on notice. There is going to be an extra bit of fire coming from all the guys, be it because of a fresh approach, a new voice, or the pressure imposed by the firing of someone in one’s vicinity. A new approach doesn’t necessarily mean more success. I don’t necessarily think the defense is going to be significantly better in its first week with a new coordinator. I expect there will be missed assignments and some growing pains. But I do think we’ll see a more disruptive defensive line that will muck things up against a disjointed Broncos offense.

item.title: ‘Biggest problem’: Evan Turner says Giannis Antetokounmpo has caused a real issue for Miami Heat now
item.description: Photo by Minas Panagiotakis/Getty Images Giannis Antetokounmpo was expected to take the Miami Heat to a whole new level when he joined them in the summer. The Heat acquired the Greek superstar in a blockbuster trade that saw Tyler Herro, Kel’el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr. and Kasparas Jakučionis go to the Milwaukee Bucks, along with the 2026 No. 13 pick, two future unprotected first-round picks (2031, 2033), a 2030 first-round swap, and a 2033 second-round pick. However, Antetokounmpo has had his struggles in Miami, and that has led to a lot of criticism coming his way from several people in the sport. Evan Turner is the latest to join the party. Evan Turner says Miami Heat have lost their culture because of Giannis Antetokounmpo Turner played for a decade in the NBA and faced the Miami Heat plenty of times. Although the players changed over the years, the 6ft 6in former small forward always noticed something about the Heat’s culture that made them a difficult team to beat. However, watching them this season, Turner believes that Miami have lost that culture of having great ball movement and being solid defensively. Why? Turner believes it is all because of Antetokounmpo. He said on SI’s Open Floor NBA talk show: “I believe when you bring over such a dominant and impactful player, you’re gonna take on a lot of the characteristics. “When it comes down to it, the presence of Giannis, I feel as though, has withdrawn from the Heat Culture and what they hang their hat on. Which is great ball movement and ‘just defence’. They’ve been terrible defensively this whole year. They’ve given up so many 120-point games. I don’t really know how to add it up.” Turner then accused the Heat of becoming “Milwaukee Bucks 2.0” because of Antetokounmpo and wondered how they could make it work. He concluded by saying: “Him going out and doing him night in and night out hasn’t been advantageous and hasn’t been great for the rest of the team, in my opinion. “You have no sniff or sign of the Heat Culture. That’s the biggest problem.” The Miami Heat have not looked great this season, but pointing the finger at just Antetokounmpo and ignoring all their other shortcomings just does not feel fair. Even if it is the Greek star’s fault, Miami would’ve known his style of play very well before acquiring him and agreeing to pay him a fortune every year. Antetokounmpo is one of the best players in the game. Instead of pointing the finger at him, the Heat should find a way to play to his strengths and get everyone firing.
